meta: Francesco Villamena's engraved title page of 1620 for La Sacra Genesi figurata, framed by winged putti and a cardinal's coat of arms.
about: Four winged putti frame a shell-decorated escutcheon on this engraved title page for La Sacra Genesi figurata. Two hover above with fruit garlands. Two stand below on a long band. A shield with the arms of a cardinal, which the museum's record spells Albrodrandini, sits at the top. The record also notes a slight pencil copy of the lower left putto in the left margin, and illegible pencil marks on the right. Francesco Villamena made the print in 1620. |

meta: Ike Taiga's mid-1700s hanging scroll of West Lake near Hangzhou, painted in ink and light color on paper.
about: Arched bridges linking small islands tell the viewer this misty lakeside is West Lake, near Hangzhou in China. Revered poets made the lake their home. The Cleveland museum names two of them. Bai Juyi lived near the water, and Lin Bu led a reclusive life on Solitary Hill. Ike Taiga painted the scroll in the mid-1700s, as one of the first Japanese artists to follow Chinese scholars who painted as amateurs. He studied images in Chinese wood-block printed books. Pavilions with tiled roofs sit along the foreground shore. |

meta: Pieter Saenredam's 1636 view inside the Great Church of St. Bavo in Haarlem, with its big organ and a woman and two children by a column.
about: A woman sits with two children beside a great column on the left. Pieter Saenredam painted the Great or Saint Bavo Church in Haarlem from the south choir aisle, looking through the choir and across to the north aisle with the big organ. On a shutter of that organ is a painted Resurrection of Christ. A small organ stands in a chapel at lower right. Saenredam signed and dated the picture on that small organ in 1636. | https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/200107963

meta: Achille Devéria's 1826 painting of Voltaire rising from his armchair to bless Benjamin Franklin's grandson in a garden.
about: Under a tree in a garden, Voltaire rises from his armchair to bless a small boy. The boy is the grandson of Benjamin Franklin, who stands beside him in a grey coat. Voltaire's niece, Madame Denis, sits nearby and watches. Achille Devéria painted the meeting in 1826. The Museum of Fine Arts of Reims holds the work. |

meta: Bartholomaeus Spranger's Ceres and Bacchus, a seventeenth-century copy of a print by Jan Harmensz Muller, now in the Cleveland Museum of Art.
about: Ceres carries a sheaf of wheat and Bacchus holds a bunch of grapes as the two walk together through a shadowed wood. The Cleveland museum says this canvas copies a print by Jan Harmensz Muller, which was itself based on a painting by Spranger. Spranger often used the pairing of these two agricultural gods. Muller's print carries a Latin motto meaning that without Ceres and Bacchus, Venus grows cold. The museum reads it as saying love cannot live without food and drink. | https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org

meta: Bernhard Strigel's Arrest of Christ, a Passion panel from an altarpiece made for the Carthusian monastery at Buxheim.
about: Armed men in red, green and white seize a haloed Christ, and a kneeling figure in green is at the lower left. Bernhard Strigel painted it as one of several Passion scenes for a polyptych, an altarpiece with many panels. The Carthusian monastery at Buxheim in Swabia commissioned the altarpiece, and it was finished by 1500. The Walters Art Museum holds four of its panels. Others are in Berlin and Augsburg. |

meta: Federico Zuccaro's Cupid and Pan, about 1600, in which Cupid pulls the god of the wild down by the ear.
about: Cupid climbs onto the back of Pan, who is on all fours, and grabs one of his ears. Onlookers react in shock, gesturing and wide-eyed. A winged allegorical figure soars above. The Getty reads Pan as carnal lust, so the struggle between the two gods stands for divine love against earthly love. The subject comes from a line by the Roman poet Virgil, Omnia vincit amor, which means Love conquers all. Federico Zuccaro painted it about 1600. |

meta: Carroll Beckwith's 1870 painting of a stone tower at Saint-Malo in Normandy under a stormy sky.
about: Dark storm clouds press down on a round stone tower rising above a quay with moored sailboats. James Carroll Beckwith made many trips to Europe and spent at least one summer in Normandy. The coastal light there inspired a series of moody paintings of dramatic ruins against restless skies. The Smithsonian museum says this one shows a fourteenth-century fortress in Saint-Malo. Beckwith put the massive structure at the top of the canvas against the stormy sky to stress its height. |

meta: Pieter de Hooch's courtyard scene with two men at a table, traced from an Amsterdam sale to the Rothschilds and the National Gallery of Art.
about: Two men sit at a small table in a brick-paved Dutch yard, one smoking a long pipe, while a woman in a red skirt stands nearby and a young girl in a bonnet waits. A sale of the Amsterdam collector Cornelis Sebille Roos's collection in 1820 included the painting. By 1842 it belonged to Baron Lionel de Rothschild. It passed down his family to Almina, Countess of Carnarvon. She sold it to the dealer Duveen Brothers in 1924. | https://github.com/NationalGalleryOfArt/opendata

meta: John Wesley Jarvis's portrait of Thomas Paine, backed by an 1836 label certifying the sitter, now in the National Gallery of Art.
about: John Wesley Jarvis painted Thomas Paine as an older man with grey hair swept back, a dark coat and a white cravat. A paper label once on the back of the original canvas is dated New York, August 1836. Signed by Jarvis and by Charles Jarvis, it certifies that the picture is a portrait of the late Thomas Paine. Christopher C. Yates owned it by 1836. It later went to James Ferguson and then to Horatio Bridge. A grandniece of Bridge's wife gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1950. | https://github.com/NationalGalleryOfArt/opendata

meta: Samuel F. B. Morse's small oil portrait of Joseph Gales, painted on wood and bought by the National Gallery of Art in 2014.
about: A small oil portrait on wood shows Joseph Gales in a dark coat and white neckcloth, turned slightly toward the viewer. Samuel F. B. Morse painted it, and the brushwork around the face and tousled hair is loose and warm. The collector Lee B. Anderson owned it, and it passed through Victor D. Spark in New York. The Corcoran Gallery of Art in Washington bought it in 1951. The National Gallery of Art acquired it in 2014. | https://github.com/NationalGalleryOfArt/opendata

meta: Giuseppe Maria Crespi's Cupids Disarming Sleeping Nymphs, an oil on copper that the Kress Foundation sold, returned and bought again.
about: Several women in flowing draperies sleep in a dark wooded landscape while small winged Cupids disarm them. Count Alessandro Contini Bonacossi of Rome sold the painting to the Samuel H. Kress Foundation in 1930. The bill of sale called it a hunting scene by G. B. Crespi. A note says it was credited back to the count a year later, yet it was bought back the year after that. The Kress Foundation gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1939. | https://github.com/NationalGalleryOfArt/opendata

meta: Gerard David's Saint Nicholas, the left panel of his Saint Anne Altarpiece, traced from Mallorca and Brussels to the National Gallery of Art.
about: A bishop in a red and gold brocade cope stands under a Gothic arch with a crosier and an open book. This is the left panel of the Saint Anne Altarpiece by Gerard David, showing Saint Nicholas. Cardinal Antonio Despuig y Dameto owned it on Mallorca, and it stayed there with the Counts of Montenegro. By 1899 it was in Brussels with Leon de Somzée. Peter A. B. Widener of Pennsylvania bought it in 1907. Joseph E. Widener gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1942. | https://github.com/NationalGalleryOfArt/opendata
dimensions:
painted surface (including addition at top): 234 x 74.9 cm (92 1/8 x 29 1/2 in.)
overall (panel): 236.1 x 75.7 cm (92 15/16 x 29 13/16 in.)

meta: Frédéric Bazille's view of the western ramparts at Aigues-Mortes, which passed from his brother's family to Paul Mellon.
about: A long fortified wall with round towers rises above a calm lagoon at Aigues-Mortes, and fishing boats lie moored at the water's edge. Bazille signed the canvas at the lower left. His brother Marc Bazille owned it first, and then Marc's daughter in Montpellier, who lent it to exhibitions in Paris and at the Royal Academy. A Paris sale in 1963 ended with Paul Mellon owning it. He gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1985. | https://github.com/NationalGalleryOfArt/opendata
credit_line: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon

meta: Domenico Quaglio's 1835 oil painting of the summer refectory in the Grand Master's Palace at Marienburg, in the Karlsruhe Kunsthalle.
about: A clergyman in a black robe gestures to a group of children beneath the tall windows and vaults of a Gothic hall. This is the summer refectory of the Grand Master's Palace at Marienburg. The Karlsruhe museum says Domenico Quaglio travelled in 1832 at the request of the Prussian crown prince, later King Friedrich Wilhelm IV. He went from Danzig to Königsberg and Tilsit to make views of central Gothic buildings. The painting is dated 1835. |

meta: William Sidney Mount's The Tough Story, a country tavern scene commissioned in 1837 by Robert Gilmor Jr. of Baltimore.
about: Three men gather around a wood stove in a country tavern, and one of them sits with a bandaged head, gesturing with a glass of liquor in his hand. Robert Gilmor Jr. of Baltimore commissioned William Sidney Mount to paint it in 1837. Gilmor's nephew Charles Smith Gilmor inherited it. A Baltimore firm sold it, and the Corcoran Gallery of Art in Washington bought it in 1874. The National Gallery of Art acquired it in 2014. | https://github.com/NationalGalleryOfArt/opendata

meta: George Caleb Bingham's Cottage Scenery, a thatched cottage that the American Art Union bought and a Georgia man won in 1845.
about: A thatched cottage with a brick chimney stands beside a dirt path, with figures at its door and a large tree shading the left side. The American Art Union in New York bought the picture from George Caleb Bingham. James D. Carhart of Macon, Georgia, won it the same year, and his family kept it. The Corcoran Gallery of Art bought it in 1961. The National Gallery of Art acquired it in 2014. | https://github.com/NationalGalleryOfArt/opendata
credit_line: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund and Gifts of Charles C. Glover,  Jr., Orme Wilson, and Mr. and Mrs. Lansdell K. Christie, 1961)

meta: Gaetano Gandolfi's 1766 painting of the Marriage at Cana, where Jesus turns water into wine at a wedding banquet.
about: A wedding banquet fills a colonnade, with musicians playing on a balcony above. Gaetano Gandolfi painted the first miracle of Christ from the Gospel of John. After the wine ran out, Jesus had six jars filled with water and turned it into wine. Here he points to the jars while his mother looks at him. Gandolfi added a man in a turban, an African servant and a pair of fighting animals. The Walters Art Museum describes these as anecdotal details. The painting is dated 1766. |

meta: Egbert Lievensz. van der Poel's 1640 view of a stairway tower in Delft, probably the scene just before William the Silent was shot.
about: A man carrying a stack of books walks down a spiral staircase toward a wooden door, and a dog waits for him on the steps. The Rijksmuseum thinks the scene shows the stairway tower of the Prinsenhof in Delft just before the assassination of William the Silent. A portrait bust stands above the door to the stairs, and a coat of arms is at upper right. Egbert Lievensz. van der Poel painted it in 1640. Halberds hang on the left wall. | https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/20026048

meta: Henri Leys's 1838 interior set in the seventeenth century, with a man reading by a table and a cat on a chair.
about: A man with a pipe in his hand reads a letter or pamphlet at a table, while a woman sits at the left doing needlework. A glass jug and a glass stand on the table. Henri Leys set this scene in the seventeenth century and signed and dated it above the cat, in 1838. A fireplace and a painting are at the left, and the cat sits on a chair at lower right. The Rijksmuseum has it on loan from the City of Amsterdam, from the A. van der Hoop bequest. | https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/20028185
